feature: Customer Portal v2 -- isolated parallel build of the Overview (/portal-v2) and the six pillar dashboards (/portal-v2/:pillar) in the new navy/journeyTokens design language. Deliberately separate routes from the live /governance, /security-overview, /m365-health, /compliance, /adoption, /licensing pages, which this build does not touch. Data comes from GET /api/portal/assessment/war-room-pillars via components/portal-v2/usePortalV2Pillars.ts, which wraps the EXISTING components/war-room/useWarRoomPillarStats.ts hook rather than reimplementing fetching, retry/backoff or scoring. Pillar identity colours and the 82 gate constant come from components/copilot-journey/journeyTokens.ts (PILLARS, COPILOT_GATE_TARGET); components/ui/score-ring.tsx is reused verbatim, with .pv2-root redefining the --status-*/--muted tokens it reads so it resolves against the navy palette.
notes: SCOPE: Overview + six pillar pages only. Change Control, SOPs & Runbooks, Risk Register, Microsoft Changes and Hold Windows are deliberately NOT built in this pass -- the existing implementations of the first four are MSP-operator-scoped (/api/msp/*, requireRole('MSPOperator') + resolveMspIdStrict) and reusing them from a customer page would leak cross-tenant data; they need new customer-scoped routes first.

THE API TESTS ARE THE REAL CONTRACT ASSERTIONS. A1-A4 exercise GET /api/portal/assessment/war-room-pillars -- the exact endpoint and payload these pages render -- so they verify the data layer independently of whether the new UI has been deployed yet.

HONEST-NULL CONTRACT: the payload's per-pillar `score` is deliberately nullable and carries an `evaluation` of scored | insufficient_data | not_evaluated (#517). The v2 pages render three different sentences for those and NEVER a red zero for a missing score. A4 asserts the field exists rather than asserting a number, because asserting a number would make this manifest fail on an honestly-unscored tenant, which is the correct product behaviour.

ENV VARS required in BuildConsole -> Settings -> Test Environment Variables: DEPLOY_URL, TEST_PORTAL_EMAIL / TEST_PORTAL_PASSWORD -- the same testbed Assessment-role account m365-health-pillar-live-scan.json and m365-health-breakdown-gate.json drive.

UI ROUTE SHAPE: msp-portal's outer WouterRouter has base '/portal' and SlugScope nests a second router at '/{slug}', so the real URL is /portal/{slug}/portal-v2. Route order in App.tsx declares '/portal-v2' BEFORE '/portal-v2/:pillar' so the index is not swallowed by the param match.
shaneapp://runTest hits the DEPLOYED build, not the local worktree -- the U* steps below only exercise the new pages once this commit is deployed to the dev server.

RUN GREEN 2026-08-19: 21/21 against the deployed dev server at commit 393afe75 (deployed via trigger-deploy-and-wait.ps1, f101d5547 -> 393afe758, 47.5s). Real values observed on screen: Copilot gate '50 / 82', Governance severity chip 'Attention required' from a real score of 56 (>=50 and <60 per journeyTokens severityForScore), and the live /governance page still rendering its own 56 unchanged (U8, the isolation guarantee).

AN EARLIER RUN OF THIS MANIFEST CAUGHT A REAL BUG, which is why the API assertions are shaped the way they are: `evaluation` is an OBJECT ({status, reason, ...}) and the first version of the v2 model declared it as a bare status string. tsc could not catch it because the type was self-declared. A4 now asserts the nested `.evaluation.status` path specifically so a regression that flattens it is caught here rather than in the UI.

SEPARATELY VERIFIED (scratch probe, not kept as steps): /portal-v2/adoption renders a real score with stats and an honest empty findings state, and /portal-v2/nonsense correctly falls through to NotFound rather than rendering an empty pillar shell.

RUN GREEN 2026-08-19: 72/72 against the deployed dev server at commit 2335caf9 (deployed via trigger-deploy-and-wait.ps1, d7a08d041 -> 2335caf90, 41.7s), covering the 25 new OV* steps for the Overshared SharePoint drill-down. Real text observed on screen: the stat card reading 'SHARING CAPABILITY Enabled ExternalUserAndGuestSharing'; Top Risks genuinely ABSENT from the DOM before the toggle and present after ('Public Team exposes the entire site to anyone…'); site 0 expanding to its real 52 admins starting 'Alex Rivera alex.rivera@tenant.com'; the convert runbook rendering 'RUNBOOK · FULL TRANSPARENCY 1. Notify all site a…'; the accept-risk drawer titled 'Accept risk — Client Deliverables (SharePoint)'; the pager stepping 'Page 1 of 16 « ‹ 1 2 ··· 16 › »' to 'Page 2 of 16 « ‹ 1 2 3 ··· 16 › »'; and the bulk list heading '23,412 sites are shared externally…'. Also verified at that commit: tsc --noEmit clean, a full vite build clean, and 17/17 on src/components/portal-v2/govOversharingData.test.ts, which pins the fixture arithmetic (124 sites / 95 links / 52 admins on site 0 / 43 Public / 16 pages) and the shared pager's window rule.

OBSERVED, NOT A REGRESSION, WORTH KNOWING: CR2 shows the fix panel reading 'Apply the recommended change' — the GENERIC FALLBACK — because govPages.ts's sharing-drift policy rows carry fixKeys (gov-drift-anon-expiry, gov-drift-default-permission, gov-drift-domain-allowlist, gov-drift-alert) that exist in neither FIX_PLAYBOOKS nor the prototype's GOV_FIXES. The gate still works end to end, which is what CR1-CR7 assert, but 'wrench fixes tied to NAMED playbooks' is currently only true on the oversharing page (OV18 asserts its real title). Writing those four playbooks is real outstanding work, not a test defect.

apiTests.name: SETUP -- log in as the designated TESTBED Assessment account; extract the bearer.
A1 -- war-room-pillars responds 200 to a CustomerUser/Assessment bearer. This is the single endpoint every v2 page reads.
A2 -- the payload carries a generatedAt stamp, which the Overview and each pillar page print as provenance rather than implying the numbers are live-to-the-second.

A3 -- pillars[0] is governance. The array is emitted in WAR_ROOM_PILLAR_KEYS order (governance, licensing, adoption, compliance, health, security, copilot), and journeyTokens' PILLAR_KEYS indexes straight into these cards by name, which is why the v2 pages reuse the pillar identity map unchanged.

A4 -- the governance card's `evaluation` is an OBJECT carrying a `status`, NOT a bare status string. This is the honest-null contract the v2 pages depend on, and asserting the nested path pins the real wire shape: a regression that flattened it back to a string would make every pillar render the wrong 'no data' copy. Asserted as exists, not as a value -- an honestly-unscored tenant must not fail this manifest.

A5 -- the copilot card rides in the SAME payload at index 6. The v2 Overview renders its score as the Copilot Gate against COPILOT_GATE_TARGET (82) rather than issuing a second request, because it is the same computePillarDisplayScore number the live surfaces use.

uiSteps.name: goto the real login URL (outer WouterRouter base = '/portal').
WAIT for the login form to hydrate before typing.
Primary login -- every downstream assertion needs a real authenticated session.
goto the v2 Overview on its isolated, slug-scoped route.
U1 -- the v2 Overview renders its own shell (proves the isolated route resolves and did not fall through to NotFound).
SHELL 1 -- the sidebar renders expanded by default (256px per the spec; the attribute is what the collapse toggle flips).
SHELL 2 -- the header's search TRIGGER is present with its Cmd-K affordance. It is a trigger, not an input -- the palette is what opens.
SHELL 3 -- the account chip renders with name and role.
SHELL 4 -- the alerts tray is CLOSED until the bell is clicked.
SHELL 5 -- the collapse toggle exists (the panel-left button the spec calls for).
SHELL 6 -- collapsing the sidebar flips it to the 76px state and hides the label text.
SHELL 7 -- collapsed: the two-line wordmark is gone (the brand mark stays), proving the expanded/collapsed branch really switched.
SHELL 8 -- restore the sidebar so later steps see the default state.
U2 -- all six pillar cards render. The governance card is asserted specifically; its presence proves PILLAR_KEYS drove the grid from the real payload.

U3 -- the Health pillar card renders. Health is the one pillar whose engine key differs (backend 'architecture' displays as 'Health', Git #1098); this proves the v2 grid uses the display taxonomy, not the engine key.

U4 -- the security pillar card renders. Security is deliberately NOT in HEALTH_PILLARS server-side (it is scored by security-engine.ts and recombined), so its presence here proves the v2 build reads the war-room payload rather than the health-engine pillar array.

goto the SECURITY pillar page. Governance now has a bespoke rebuilt dashboard, so Security is the pillar that still exercises the GENERIC pillar page -- which is exactly what needs regression cover, since the other five pillars all render through it.
U5 -- the generic pillar page renders its heading from the real payload.
U6 -- the generic pillar page prints run provenance: which run the findings belong to, or an explicit statement that no completed run backs them. Either way it never implies numbers it does not have.
goto the rebuilt Governance pillar dashboard.
G1 -- the Governance hero renders with the design's own score ring (a bare numeral in mono, not the shared ScoreRing's percentage).
G2 -- the cluster area-card grid renders. Governance deliberately has NO finding rows -- the prototype builds governanceRows but never renders them -- so the area grid IS the pillar's content.
G3 -- an area tile links into the drill-down.
G4 -- the drill-down renders its heading from the page data.
G5 -- the Graph/PowerShell provenance block is present (the drill-down template's second section).
G6 -- the tenant-policy block renders with its real setting names.
CR1 -- THE GATE, END TO END. A wrench on a policy row opens the fix panel on that fixKey.
CR2 -- the fix panel opened on the right playbook.
uiSteps.textContains: How would you like to handle this?

uiSteps.name: CR3 -- choosing the Graph route goes to the CHANGE REQUEST step, not straight to the change. This is the gate's whole point: nothing runs without a CR.

uiSteps.name: CR5 -- submit is GATED on the confirmation checkbox. Ticking it is what arms the button.

goto the Overshared SharePoint drill-down. Before this pass the route rendered NotFound: 13 of the 14 area tiles pointed at /portal-v2/governance/<area> and only sharing-drift existed in GOV_PAGES.
OV1 -- the page renders its own heading, not NotFound.
OV2 -- the stat cards carry the prototype's real values, including the tenant setting name the whole finding hangs on.

OV4 -- open Top Risks.

uiSteps.textContains: Anonymous links found with edit access, not just view

uiSteps.name: OV6 -- the Affected Sites evidence list renders the written-out sites.
OV7 -- the visibility filter really filters, it does not just restyle. Under 'Public' the 124-site set drops to 43, which pulls sites off later pages onto page 1.

OV8 -- proof the window moved: 'HR Onboarding #9' is site id 8, which is on page 2 under 'All' and can only appear on page 1 once the three Private sites ahead of it are filtered out. Asserted positively rather than as an absence, because uiStep `expect` supports textContains / textPrefixOfAny only -- a 'contains none' field would be silently ignored and the step would pass on element presence alone.

OV10 -- expand a site row.
OV11 -- the expanded row shows the real principal counts, not a placeholder. 4 named admins + 48 generated staff = 52.

OV14 -- and it carries the SYNTHESISED verification step buildStepRows appends to every runbook: a runbook is not complete when the work is done, only when the scan says it took.
